```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The window controls how local the trend is and how far it is extrapolated.
Short windows adapt to local movement but estimate the line from less data;
long windows use more observations but impose linearity over a longer span.
The main window-sensitivity examples use estimand-specific calibration.

```{r}
library(eventsurvey)
library(dplyr)

dat <- sample_data
windows <- 3:7
fits <- lapply(windows, function(s) {
  eventsurvey(y ~ day, dat, window = s)
})
sensitivity <- lapply(seq_along(fits), function(i) {
  fits[[i]]$estimate |>
    mutate(window = windows[i], .before = 1)
}) |>
  bind_rows()

sensitivity |>
  select(window, effect, bias_bound, conf_low, conf_high)
```

Changing the window changes the counterfactual, number of rolling exercises,
bias bound, and sampling uncertainty. Interpret them jointly.

Useful prespecified checks include plausible window lengths, including versus
excluding the event period, restrictions motivated by known fieldwork breaks,
and outcomes or subgroups chosen before inspecting results. Do not select the
window that produces the smallest p-value or narrowest interval.

## Compare calibration assumptions

The default `calibration = "estimand"` matches references to daily and average
targets. The earlier `"pooled"` option uses all individual errors. Keep the
outcome, target periods, and model fixed when comparing these assumptions:

```{r calibration-comparison}
calibrations <- c("estimand", "pooled")
calibration_fits <- lapply(calibrations, function(method) {
  eventsurvey(y ~ day, dat, window = 6, calibration = method)
})
lapply(seq_along(calibration_fits), function(i) {
  calibration_fits[[i]]$estimate |>
    mutate(
      method = if (i == 1L) "Main: estimand-specific" else "Comparison: pooled",
      .before = 1
    )
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  select(method, effect, bias_bound, n_reference, conf_low, conf_high)
```

The default average bound uses the largest absolute signed window-average
error; pooled calibration uses the largest absolute individual error.
`n_reference` counts the contrasts used for the average interval. Daily
results in each fit's `days` table use matching horizons under the default.

With the same reference windows, estimand-specific intervals are contained
in the pooled intervals, under tighter target-specific bias restrictions.
Sparse schedules can produce different reference-window sets, so this nesting
is not guaranteed. Choose the primary assumption before inspecting whether
an interval excludes zero; see [Methodology](methodology.html).
